title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: The root cause of this issue was a latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system that resulted in an incorrect empty DNS record for the service’s regional endpoint (dynamodb.us-east-1.amazonaws.com) that the automation failed to repair.
detection_note: By 12:38 AM on October 20, our engineers had identified DynamoDB’s DNS state as the source of the outage.
notes: Race between DNS Enactors left empty Route53 record; cascaded to EC2 launches (DWFM) and NLB health checks.

title: Summary of the Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Service Event in Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: The root cause of this event was the cell management system’s behavior in managing the novel workload profile of one of these internal cells. Specifically, unlike workload profiles in other Kinesis Data Streams cells, one of the internal workloads on the impacted cell had a very large number of very low-throughput shards which caused the cell management system to behave incorrectly and triggered this event.
detection_note: Engineering teams were immediately engaged and began investigating the affected cell.
notes: Routine deployment (hosts taken in/out of service) exposed cell-manager flaw on newly migrated internal cell; trigger borderline latent_bug.

title: Summary of the AWS Lambda Service Event in Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: At 11:49 AM PDT, the Lambda Frontend fleet, while adding additional compute capacity to handle the increase in service traffic, crossed a capacity threshold that had previously never been reached within a single cell. This triggered a latent software defect which caused Lambda Execution Environments to be successfully allocated for incoming requests, but never fully utilized by the Lambda Frontend.
detection_note: By 12:26 PM PDT, engineers had identified the latent software defect and the impact on the provisioning of underlying compute capacity.
notes: Normal daily traffic scaling crossed untested cell size; STS, Console, Connect, EventBridge impacted.

title: Summary of the AWS Service Event in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: At 7:30 AM PST, an automated activity to scale capacity of one of the AWS services hosted in the main AWS network triggered an unexpected behavior from a large number of clients inside the internal network. This resulted in a large surge of connection activity that overwhelmed the networking devices between the internal network and the main AWS network, resulting in delays for communication between these networks.
detection_note: This congestion immediately impacted the availability of real-time monitoring data for our internal operations teams, which impaired their ability to find the source of congestion and resolve it. Operators instead relied on logs to understand what was happening and initially identified elevated internal DNS errors.
notes: Automated scaling activity hit latent client back-off bug; internal DNS errors part of chain; duration to network recovery (STS/API GW longer).

title: Summary of AWS Direct Connect Event in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: We have now confirmed that this event was caused by a latent issue within the network device operating system.
detection_note: On September 2, 2021 at 7:30 AM JST, internal alarms alerted AWS engineers to elevated packet loss for Direct Connect customers connecting to the Tokyo Region.
notes: Network OS/new protocol rolled out months earlier hit by specific customer packet signature; change_triggered true because that rollout is named in chain.

title: Summary of the Amazon Kinesis Event in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: The trigger, though not root cause, for the event was a relatively small addition of capacity that began to be added to the service at 2:44 AM PST, finishing at 3:47 AM PST.
detection_note: At 5:15 AM PST, the first alarms began firing for errors on putting and getting Kinesis records.
notes: Capacity add pushed front-end servers past OS thread limit; Cognito, CloudWatch etc. impacted.

title: Summary of the Amazon EC2 and Amazon EBS Service Event in the Tokyo (AP-NORTHEAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: This event was caused by a failure of our datacenter control system, which is used to control and optimize the various cooling systems used in our datacenters.
notes: Third-party control-system bug during host failover; PLCs unresponsive, cooling shut down, servers overheated.

title: Summary of the Amazon EC2 DNS Resolution Issues in the Asia Pacific (Seoul) Region (AP-NORTHEAST-2)
root_cause_quote: The root cause of DNS resolution issues was a configuration update which incorrectly removed the setting that specifies the minimum healthy hosts for the EC2 DNS resolver fleet in the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region.
detection_note: At 8:21 AM KST, the engineering team was alerted to the DNS resolution issue within the AP-NORTHEAST-2 Region and immediately began working on resolution.
notes: Missing min-healthy-hosts setting fell back to low default; resolver fleet downscaled.

title: Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
root_cause_quote: At 9:37AM PST, an authorized S3 team member using an established playbook executed a command which was intended to remove a small number of servers for one of the S3 subsystems that is used by the S3 billing process. Unfortunately, one of the inputs to the command was entered incorrectly and a larger set of servers was removed than intended.
notes: Mistyped capacity-removal command forced full restart of index/placement subsystems; SHD itself depended on S3.

title: Summary of the AWS Service Event in the Sydney Region
root_cause_quote: At 10:25 PM PDT on June 4th, our utility provider suffered a loss of power at a regional substation as a result of severe weather in the area. This failure resulted in a total loss of utility power to multiple AWS facilities. In one of the facilities, our power redundancy didn't work as designed, and we lost power to a significant number of instances in that Availability Zone.
notes: Voltage sag drained DRUPS before generators engaged; DNS errors and a latent instance-management bug slowed recovery.

title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption and Related Impacts in the US-East Region
root_cause_quote: But, on Sunday morning, a portion of the metadata service responses exceeded the retrieval and transmission time allowed by storage servers. As a result, some of the storage servers were unable to obtain their membership data, and removed themselves from taking requests.
detection_note: By 2:37am PDT, the error rate in customer requests to DynamoDB had risen far beyond any level experienced in the last 3 years, finally stabilizing at approximately 55%.
notes: Brief network disruption plus GSI-inflated membership lists overloaded under-provisioned metadata service; retry storm.

title: Summary of the Amazon EC2, Amazon EBS, and Amazon RDS Service Event in the EU West Region
root_cause_quote: The service disruption began at 10:41 AM PDT on August 7th when our utility provider suffered a failure of a 110kV 10 megawatt transformer. This failure resulted in a total loss of electricity supply to all of their customers connected to this transformer, including a significant portion of the affected AWS Availability Zone.
notes: PES index lists Aug 7, 2014 but report calls Aug 7 a Sunday (2011, Dublin). PLC failed to sync generators; multi-day EBS recovery; separate EBS snapshot-deletion bug.

title: Summary of the Amazon SimpleDB Service Disruption
root_cause_quote: In this event, multiple storage nodes became unavailable simultaneously in a single data center (after power was lost to the servers on which these nodes lived).
notes: Year from PES index. Power loss surged lock-service load; handshake timeout too low, nodes removed themselves.

title: Summary of the December 17th event in the South America Region (SA-EAST-1)
root_cause_quote: On December 17th at 10:05PM PST, the impacted Availability Zone lost utility power due to a fault that happened at the substation of the local utility provider.
notes: Breaker opened and second generator failed; automated generator control system malfunctioned; manual network config error caused 20 min regional degradation.

title: Summary of the December 24, 2012 Amazon ELB Service Event in the US-East Region
root_cause_quote: The data was deleted by a maintenance process that was inadvertently run against the production ELB state data.
detection_note: It was when the ELB technical team started digging deeply into these degraded load balancers that the team identified the missing ELB state data as the root cause of the service disruption.
notes: Developer with persistent prod access ran maintenance process against prod; duration to 'almost all' LBs restored.

title: Summary of the October 22, 2012 AWS Service Event in the US-East Region
root_cause_quote: The root cause of the problem was a latent bug in an operational data collection agent that runs on the EBS storage servers.
detection_note: While we monitor aggregate memory consumption on each EBS Server, our monitoring failed to alarm on this memory leak.
notes: Initiating event: DNS update during a server replacement failed to propagate, triggering latent memory leak; root cause stated as latent bug.

title: Summary of the AWS Service Event in the US East Region
root_cause_quote: At 7:24pm PDT, a large voltage spike was experienced by the electrical switching equipment in two of the US East-1 datacenters supporting a single Availability Zone. All utility electrical switches in both datacenters initiated transfer to generator power. In one of the datacenters, the transfer completed without incident. In the other, the generators started successfully, but each generator independently failed to provide stable voltage as they were brought into service.
notes: Electrical storm; generators failed to stabilise; duration 8:04pm power loss to 90% EBS volumes back at 2:45am.

title: Summary of the Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS Service Disruption in the US East Region
root_cause_quote: At 12:47 AM PDT on April 21st, a network change was performed as part of our normal AWS scaling activities in a single Availability Zone in the US East Region. The configuration change was to upgrade the capacity of the primary network. During the change, one of the standard steps is to shift traffic off of one of the redundant routers in the primary EBS network to allow the upgrade to happen. The traffic shift was executed incorrectly and rather than routing the traffic to the other router on the primary network, the traffic was routed onto the lower capacity redundant EBS network.
detection_note: Initially, our alarming was not fine-grained enough for this EBS control plane API and the launch errors were overshadowed by the general error from the degraded EBS cluster.
notes: Mis-executed network traffic shift caused EBS re-mirroring storm; borderline maintenance_op. Duration to Apr 24 12:30 PM.

title: Network connectivity – Issues accessing resources in West US
root_cause_quote: On 23 July 2026, a break-fix repair was initiated on an optical device to address a network reliability risk. A defect in our blast radius analysis system incorrectly expanded the scope of the repair event to include all optical devices egressing a specific datacenter.
detection_note: Service alerts fired at 14:45 UTC, one minute after impact, but the routing anomaly was initially mis-triaged as a WAN issue.
notes: Automated break-fix over-scoped to a whole datacenter; per-device safety checks missed the aggregate effect.

title: Azure OpenAI Service – Latency and intermittent failures in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: The triggering condition was a change in an upstream API layer used by a Microsoft first-party workload, Microsoft 365, which relies on Azure OpenAI for some request processing scenarios, including Copilot-related experiences. This change altered how capacity-related failures were surfaced to higher layers in the request path.
detection_note: 09:39 UTC on 29 May 2026 – Automated monitoring detected a drop in request success rates and initiated incident investigation.
notes: Upstream change made failures look retriable; up to 48 retries per request overloaded the AOAI routing layer. First mitigation targeted the wrong feature.

title: Azure OpenAI – GPT-5.2 availability degradation in 7 regions
root_cause_quote: A recent update to the Azure OpenAI GPT 5.2 model introduced a configuration change that was not compatible with the version of the model engine code running in production.
detection_note: 00:19 UTC on 10 March 2026 – We detected the issue via service monitoring.
notes: Config/engine version mismatch; early SDP stages had too few model instances to surface it; 400s not monitored as service-side errors.

title: Power event impacting multiple services – West US
root_cause_quote: During this incident, although utility power was still active, an electrical failure in an onsite transformer resulted in the loss of utility power to the datacenter. Although generators started as designed, a cascading failure within a control system prevented the automated transfer of load from utility power to generator power.
detection_note: 08:07 UTC on 07 February 2026 – Datacenter and engineering teams engaged and initiated coordinated investigation across power, network, storage, and compute recovery workstreams.
notes: Transformer failure plus generator transfer control failure; UPS depleted; two storage scale units slow to boot.

title: Virtual Machines, Managed identities for Azure resources, and dependent services – Service management issues in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: Due to a data synchronization problem in the targeting logic, the policy was incorrectly applied to a subset of storage accounts that are intentionally configured to allow anonymous read access for platform functionality.
detection_note: 18:29 UTC on 02 February 2026 – Internal service monitoring detected a subset of regions having an increasing number of control plane failures.
notes: Security policy job blocked VM extension storage; on recovery a retry surge saturated Managed Identity backend. GitHub Actions also hit.

title: Azure Resource Manager – Service management failures affecting Azure Government
root_cause_quote: On 08 December 2025, an inadvertent automated key rotation resulted in ARM failures to fetch authorization policies that are needed to evaluate access.
detection_note: 11:07 EST on 08 December 2025 – Engineering was engaged to investigate based on automated alerts.
notes: Cosmos DB account key wrongly onboarded with auto-rotation enabled; credential (key, not TLS cert). Same issue hit Azure China ~3h earlier.

title: Azure Front Door – Connectivity issues across multiple regions
root_cause_quote: A specific sequence of customer configuration changes, performed across two different control plane build versions, resulted in incompatible customer configuration metadata being generated. These customer configuration changes themselves were valid and non-malicious – however they produced metadata that, when deployed to edge site servers, exposed a latent bug in the data plane.
detection_note: The issue started at 15:41 UTC and was detected by monitoring at 15:48 UTC, prompting our investigation.
notes: Async data plane crash let bad metadata pass staged protection and into LKG snapshot. Customer-initiated changes; provider build versions in chain.

title: Azure Front Door – Access issues in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: On 09 October 2025, we initiated a cleanup of the affected tenant configuration with the erroneous metadata. Since the automated protection system was blocking the impacted customer tenant profile updates in the initial stage, we temporarily bypassed it to allow the cleanup of the tenant configuration to proceed.
detection_note: 08:13 UTC on 09 October 2025 – Our telemetry detected resource availability loss across multiple AFD edge sites.
notes: Manual cleanup bypassed protection; bad metadata triggered known control-plane-version data plane bug; ~26% of AFD in Europe/Africa hit.

title: Network Connectivity – Multiple services impacted in Switzerland North
root_cause_quote: A planned configuration change was made to the certificates used to authorize the communication for our software load balancer infrastructure that routes traffic for services in the Switzerland North region. One of the new certificates contained a malformed value that was not identified during the validation process.
detection_note: 00:08 UTC on 27 September 2025 – The issue was detected via our automated monitoring.
notes: Malformed cert change took an expedited path across multiple AZs without health safeguards; some VMs needed manual recovery.

title: Service management operations failures in East US 2
root_cause_quote: A recent change to Allocator behavior—designed to improve how the service handles heavy traffic— had been progressively rolled out over the prior two months, expanding to broader regions in early September. This update introduced a new throttling pattern that had performed effectively elsewhere.
detection_note: 09:13 UTC on 10 September 2025 – Monitoring systems observed a spike in allocation failure rates for Virtual Machines, triggering an alert and prompting teams to investigate.
notes: New throttling logic plus a performance issue drove aggressive retries; failover to AZ02 overloaded it; large backlog.

title: Microsoft Entra ID – DNS authentication failures using Seamless SSO and Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
root_cause_quote: As part of an ongoing maintenance effort, a change was made which inadvertently removed an intermediate DNS record and associated traffic manager used in the mentioned scenarios.
detection_note: 17:18 UTC on 25 February 2025 – Investigation started based on internal DNS reachability monitor failures.
notes: IPv6 cleanup removed in-use record; drift detection defect and mis-scored high-risk review let it pass. Seamless SSO / Connect Sync.

title: Networking issues impacting Azure Services in East US 2
root_cause_quote: Around 22:31 UTC on 08 January, during an operation to enable a feature, a manual recycling of internal PubSub replicas on certain metadata partitions was required. This recycling operation should have been completed in ‘series’ to ensure that data quorum for the partition is maintained. In this case, recycling was executed across the replicas in ‘parallel’, causing the partition to lose quorum.
detection_note: The issue was detected by monitoring on the PubSub service at 22:44 UTC, with impacted services raising alerts shortly thereafter.
notes: Lost index data on 3 partitions; ~60% of network configs not delivered in AZ01; ~50h impact.

title: Azure Storage – Unreachable Blob and Data Lake storage accounts in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: The incident was caused by an unintentional deletion of Traffic Manager profiles for the impacted storage accounts.
detection_note: 13 November 2024 @ 01:24 UTC – First customer report of issues, on-call engineering team began to investigate.
notes: Decommissioning of a deprecated service's subscriptions deleted Traffic Manager (DNS-based) profiles; detected via customer report.

title: Azure Front Door – Intermittent issues with Microsoft services using AFD
root_cause_quote: This incident was triggered by an internal service team doing a routine configuration change to their AFD profile for modifying an internal-only AFD feature. This change included an erroneous configuration file that resulted in high memory allocation rates on a subset of the AFD servers – specifically, servers that deliver traffic for an internal Microsoft customer profile.
detection_note: 18:25 UTC – Internal monitoring detected the issue and alerted our teams to investigate.
notes: Resource exhaustion then a latent client bug caused a 25x request storm; SDP had no observable failure signal.

title: Azure Front Door – Connectivity issues in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: Between 10:15 and 10:45 UTC, a volumetric distributed TCP SYN flood DDoS attack occurred at multiple Azure Front Door and CDN sites.
detection_note: 11:47 UTC on 30 July 2024 – Our Azure Portal team detected initial service degradation and began to investigate.
notes: Main impact came as DDoS mitigation disengaged and a site with power-related control plane failure kept routing via DDoS path; duration includes low-rate tail to 19:43.

title: Storage – Impact to multiple services in Central US
root_cause_quote: Due to recent changes in the network configuration of those file servers, some became inaccessible from the server which was generating the allow list. The workflow which generates the list did not detect the ‘missing’ source files, and published an allow list with incomplete VM Host address range information to all Storage scale units in the region.
detection_note: As the allow list update was being published in the Central US region, our service monitoring began to detect VM availability dropping, and our engineering teams were engaged.
notes: Incomplete storage allow-list pushed region-wide without SDP health checks. Same day as, but unrelated to, the CrowdStrike event.

title: Azure OpenAI Service – Errors in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: As part of the ongoing effort to clean up unused resources to overcome subscription limits and to reduce security vulnerability surface areas, a change was made to the global configuration file – to remove the 14 resource groups that were deemed unused. This change took effect soon after it was committed, and all resources in those resource groups were deleted in a short span of time, resulting in the cascade of failures that caused the incident.
detection_note: 00:05 UTC on 13 July 2024 – Service monitoring detected failure rates going above defined thresholds, alerting our engineers who began an investigation.
notes: Automation config drift: resource groups thought unused held GPU VMs and model endpoints; 14 of 28 AOAI regions hit.

title: DNS resolution issues impacted Azure in China
root_cause_quote: During this process, ownership for two critical system domains for Azure in China were misattributed, and as a result, were flagged as potential candidates for decommission.
detection_note: 04:37 CST on 23 April 2024 - Our internal monitors alerted us to degradation in the service and created Incident.
notes: Decommission workflow switched nameservers of chinacloudapp.cn / chinacloudsites.cn to inactive servers; tool not scoped to Azure China zones; DNS caching prolonged recovery.

title: Network connectivity - Multiple services impacted in South Africa North and South Africa West
root_cause_quote: Before our capacity additions from February had come online, on 14 March we experienced additional multiple concurrent fiber cable cuts, this time on the west coast of Africa – which further reduced the total network capacity for our Azure regions in South Africa. These cable cuts were due to a subsea seismic event (likely an earthquake and/or mudslide) which impacted multiple subsea systems – one of which is used by Microsoft.
notes: Earlier Red Sea cuts had removed east coast capacity; west coast seismic cuts plus a line card optic failure caused congestion.

title: Azure Resource Manager - Services impacted by ARM failures
root_cause_quote: On 21 January 2024, an internal maintenance process made a configuration change to an internal tenant which was enrolled in this preview. This triggered the latent code defect and caused ARM nodes, which are designed to restart periodically, to fail repeatedly upon startup.
detection_note: At 01:59 UTC, our monitoring detected a decrease in availability, and we began an investigation.
notes: Latent defect in 2020 CAE preview code; node loss then retry feedback loop (20x traffic in West Europe); Key Vault latent bug extended impact.

title: Services impacted after power/cooling issue - Australia East
root_cause_quote: Starting at approximately 08:41 UTC on 30 August 2023, a utility voltage sag was caused by a lightning strike on electrical infrastructure approximately 18 miles from the impacted Availability Zone of the Australia East region. The voltage sag caused cooling system chillers for multiple datacenters to shut down.
notes: 13 chillers failed to auto-restart; last five too hot to restart. Most services back by 22:40 UTC 30 Aug; duration is to full mitigation 3 Sep.

title: Azure Portal - Errors accessing the Azure portal
root_cause_quote: Upon further investigation, we have determined the anomalous traffic spikes to be Layer 7 distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.
detection_note: We were alerted by our internal monitoring of the traffic spikes impacting the availability of the Azure Portal.
notes: HTTP floods with cache-bypass techniques overloaded Azure Portal origin servers.

title: Azure Resource Manager – West Europe
root_cause_quote: There are several factors which contribute to increasing the feedback on this loop, however the ultimate trigger was the recent introduction of a cache used to reduce the time spent parsing complex feature flag definitions in hot loops.
detection_note: At 02:41 UTC we were alerted to a drop in regional availability for Azure Resource Manager in West Europe. This was 21 minutes after the first measurable deviation from nominal performance
notes: Spin-lock contention in new feature-flag cache saturated CPU; retries amplified. Passed four days of SDP in other regions.

title: Multi-service outage – Asia-Pacific Area
root_cause_quote: At 15:17 UTC on 7 February 2023, a utility voltage dip event occurred on the power grid, affecting a single Availability Zone in the Southeast Asia region. Power management systems managed the voltage dip as designed, however a subset of chiller units that provide cooling to the datacenter tripped and shut down.
notes: Chiller failure in one SEA AZ; unexpected ARM/BCDR impact and extended SQL Database recovery.

title: Azure Networking – Global WAN issues
root_cause_quote: This change added a command to purge the IGP database – however, the command operates differently based on router manufacturer. Routers from two of our manufacturers limit execution to the local router, while those from a third manufacturer execute across all IGP joined routers, ordering them all to recompute their IGP topology databases.
detection_note: Our monitoring detected DNS and WAN issues starting at 07:11 UTC.
notes: Madrid WAN capacity add with an untested SOP change; vendor-specific command recomputed IGP across the global WAN.

title: Multiple services – Power/cooling issues in West US 2
root_cause_quote: A severe thunderstorm produced lightning strikes, resulting in utility power disturbances across multiple datacenter facilities serving the West US 2 region.
detection_note: 04:24 UTC on 29 May 2026 – Customer impact began; our monitoring produced thermal alerts as temperatures rose due to reduced cooling functionality.
notes: Voltage sag/swell put cooling components into protective lockout across two AZs; manual cooling restarts; long storage validation.

title: Multiple services – Control plane issues in East US
root_cause_quote: Our post incident investigations confirmed that a latent regression in a recently deployed version of the PubSub service exacerbated the replica build times for the large Availability Zones of this region. This regression also contributed to the failure of the failover process, as it increased contention and reduced the service’s ability to build replicas under these conditions successfully.
detection_note: 11:38 UTC on 24 April 2026 – We detected an issue in AZ-01.
notes: Lock contention on a PubSub partition, failed failover; staged rollbacks across AZs were slow and one was incomplete.

title: Entra Privileged Identity Management – Customers experiencing API failures
root_cause_quote: As part of ongoing work to improve how the PIM service stores and manages data, configuration changes which manage the backend databases were deployed incrementally using safe deployment practices. The rollout progressed successfully through multiple rings, with no detected errors and all monitored signals remaining within healthy thresholds. When the deployment reached a ring operating under higher workload, the additional per-request processing increased demand on the underlying infrastructure that hosts the API which manages connections to the backend databases.
notes: CPU rose without tripping request-count throttles; DB connection pool exhausted. Impact began ~2.5 days after reaching the heavy ring.

title: Azure Resource Manager – Service management failures affecting Azure in China
root_cause_quote: On 08 December 2025, an inadvertent automated key rotation resulted in ARM failures to fetch authorization policies that are needed to evaluate access.
detection_note: 16:59 CST on 08 December 2025 – Engineering was engaged to investigate based on automated alerts.
notes: Azure China twin of the Azure Government ARM key-rotation incident (separate PIR); cert_involved=credential (account key).

title: Thermal event impacting multiple services in AZ01 – West Europe
root_cause_quote: The incident was triggered by a voltage sag in the utility grid, which caused cooling units to shut down and temperatures to rise above normal thresholds in a datacenter located in Physical Availability Zone 01 in the West Europe region.
detection_note: 16:55 UTC on 5 November 2025 – Datacenter monitoring detected temperature breaches and triggered thermal alerts.
notes: Sag exposed unknown hardware issue preventing cooling auto-restart; storage scale units shut down.

title: Azure Portal and other management portals – Access issues in multiple regions
root_cause_quote: Automation scripts were used to update the traffic load balancing configuration to split traffic across multiple routes. However, the scripts inadvertently removed a configuration value, because the script used an API version that predated the introduction of that value.
detection_note: 19:44 UTC on 09 October 2025 – Initial automated alerts were triggered.
notes: Follow-on to AFD QNBQ-5W8: while restoring traffic to AFD after BCDR, scripts dropped a config value; portals failed.

title: Network Connectivity – Availability issues in East US
root_cause_quote: At 13:37 UTC on 18 March 2025, a drilling operation near one of our network paths accidentally struck fiber used by Microsoft, causing an unplanned disruption to datacenter connectivity within AZ03.
detection_note: Our monitoring systems identified the impact immediately, so our on-call engineers engaged to investigate.
notes: Third-party fiber cut plus router already down for repair; auto-mitigation tool hit lock contention and left capacity un-isolated, causing a second impact window.

title: Network Connectivity – Toronto edge site issues
root_cause_quote: While we were performing an initial investigation into the cause of device failure, at 16:22 UTC the redundant device also experienced a hardware failure, due to a similar memory issue on the line cards - the line cards restarted, and did not initialize properly after startup, to forward traffic.
detection_note: 16:43 UTC on 3 March 2025 – First automated alert raised of potential issues, however the scope of impact was not evident from the alert or initial investigations.
notes: Both paired Toronto edge routers failed on line-card memory; line-card memory was not monitored.

title: Services impacted after zonal power issue – South Central US
root_cause_quote: This incident was initially triggered by a utility power loss, itself caused by a localized ground fault – in which a high voltage underground line failed.
detection_note: 18:45 UTC on 26 December 2024 – Technicians from datacenter operations team engaged.
notes: UPS battery faults in one data hall during generator transfer; one storage scale unit needed hardware replacement.

title: Azure Resource Manager – Issues in Azure US Government regions
root_cause_quote: Upon investigating, we discovered that a backend Cosmos DB was misconfigured to block legitimate access from Azure Resource Manager (ARM).
detection_note: This issue was initially flagged by our monitors detecting success rate failures.
notes: Misattributed Cosmos DB account had local auth disabled in a Secure Future Initiative sweep; global setting hit all Gov regions.

title: Azure Virtual Desktop – Unable to create new connections, impacting US regions
root_cause_quote: We determined that this incident was caused by a degradation in the redo process on one of the secondary copies servicing the US geography, which caused failures to access service resources.
detection_note: At 18:46 UTC on 16 September 2024, our internal telemetry system raised alarms about the redo log on one of our read replicas being several hours behind.
notes: SQL readable-secondary redo stalled under Monday workload; bug fix pending.

title: Azure Resource Manager – Control plane issues in China North 3
root_cause_quote: During a certificate rotation, the processes tracking these background operations were repeatedly crashing. While background jobs were still being processed, these crashes caused significant delays and an increasing backlog of jobs.
notes: Cert rotation for job-state encryption exposed a latent bug in the re-encryption path; mitigated by rollback.

title: Managed Identities for Azure resources – Failures in Australia East
root_cause_quote: Believing the deployment to have completed, a service engineer initiated the switch to move to automatic keys for the Australia East storage infrastructure, immediately causing the key to roll over.
detection_note: This incident was detected within three minutes by internal monitoring of both the Managed Identity service, and other dependent services in Azure.
notes: Region pinned to an older build; tooling reported success; key rollover broke MSI storage access. cert_involved=credential (key).

title: Azure Database for MySQL/MariaDB in West US, Azure Databricks in 3 regions
root_cause_quote: Due to a procedural error, the new connections were erroneously routed to a newly built gateway ring whose configuration was incomplete.
detection_note: As a result, the issue went undetected from service telemetry, until we received reports from internal teams about unreachable databases.
notes: DNS cutover during gateway hardware refresh pointed to an unready ring with no monitoring yet.

title: Services impacted by power, BIOS, and Virtual Machine issues – East US
root_cause_quote: Although we have redundant UPS systems in place for added resilience, this incident was initially triggered by a UPS rectifier failure on a Primary UPS.
detection_note: 16 September 2023 @ 07:33 UTC - Initial customer impact to SQL DB detected via monitoring.
notes: STS stagger logic blocked transfer back to redundant UPS; then BIOS and VM recovery issues.

title: Azure Monitor - Logs data access issues
root_cause_quote: A code deployment for the Azure Container Apps service was started on 3 July 2023 via the normal Safe Deployment Practices (SDP), first rolling out to Azure canary and staging regions. This version contained a misconfiguration that blocked the service from starting normally.
detection_note: The impact on the telemetry control plane grew slowly and did not create problems that were detected until 12:30 UTC on 6 July 2023.
notes: Crash-looping Container Apps bootstrap restarted telemetry agents every 5-10s, overloading the telemetry control plane used by Azure Monitor.

title: Networking fiber cut - West Europe
root_cause_quote: Due to a fiber cut caused by severe weather conditions in the Netherlands, 25% of network links between two campuses of West Europe datacenters became unavailable.
detection_note: Network alerting services indicated a fiber cut at 07:22 UTC and a congestion alert triggered at 07:46 UTC.
notes: Links already above design utilization; capacity augment delayed after VLB8-1Z0.

title: Networking connectivity issues - West Europe
root_cause_quote: Shortly before the start time of this incident, a new network topology description was added into the network automation systems that manage the West Europe region. This new topology included links that were about to be added to the network to increase the capacity in West Europe, but the physical links had not yet been connected or turned on. This network topology description incorrectly listed these links as being ‘Production’.
notes: Automation shut down LAGs containing not-yet-connected 'Production' links until safety thresholds stopped it.

title: Azure Storage - West Europe
root_cause_quote: A new configuration was rolled out to improve the throttling algorithm.
detection_note: Automated monitoring alerts were triggered, and engineers were immediately engaged to assess issues that the service-specific alert reported.
notes: Throttling config over-throttled storage accounts on a few scale units; found mid-SDP.

title: Service management issues - East US 2
root_cause_quote: During this incident, one of the partitions associated with physical AZ-02 experienced data access issues at 05:55 UTC on 31 January 2023, because the underlying data store had exhausted an internal resource limit.
detection_note: Automated monitoring alerts were triggered, and engineers were immediately engaged to assess the issue.
notes: Second partition failed; cache restart plus resource creation policy blocked all new VM creates in the AZ.

title: Intermittent networking issues - South Central US
root_cause_quote: During this incident, a single router in the RNG experienced a hardware fault, causing a fraction of network packets to be dropped.
detection_note: Our synthetic probe-based monitoring fired an alert at 17:58 UTC, which helped to narrow down the potential causal location to the RNG.
notes: No known signature for the hardware fault delayed automated detection.

title: Single zone power event – West Europe
root_cause_quote: We determined that an issue occurred during a planned power maintenance. While all server racks have redundant dual feeds, one feed was powered down for maintenance, and a failure in the redundant feed caused a shutdown of the affected racks.
detection_note: The issue was detected by the datacenter operation team performing the maintenance at the time.
notes: PDU breakers left at 160A (vs 380A) from earlier heat-load tests tripped when the other feed was removed.

title: Enrolling new certificates / Provisioning new resources - Azure Public / Government / China
root_cause_quote: Due to a latent performance bug in the RA, inadvertently introduced in the past month as part of a feature enhancement, the rate of new incoming requests was greater than the rate at which requests could be processed from the queue.
detection_note: The issue was detected via our internal monitoring and the relevant engineering team was engaged within one minute of the alert firing.
notes: Brief internal CA degradation queued a renewal burst; RA bug plus throttle-driven retries blocked cert issuance for provisioning.

title: Azure Cosmos DB - East US
root_cause_quote: On 26 October, a configuration change was applied to the Azure Load Balancer. This change resulted in intermittent network connectivity issues, from which the system can normally recover. However, the diagnostic change resulted in higher-than-expected time spent in the Kernel, which resulted in spikes of high CPU utilization across the cluster.
detection_note: Our monitors alerted us to the impact on this cluster.
notes: LB config change interacted with an earlier Cosmos DB gateway diagnostics change; accounts offloaded to other clusters.

title: Azure Front Door - Connectivity Issues
root_cause_quote: At this stage in our investigation, we believe that all three traffic spikes were malicious HTTPS flood attacks.
detection_note: As our telemetry alerted us regarding impact on availability, we manually intervened.
notes: Layer 7 floods plus legitimate ramp-up and retries took some AFD environments offline; attribution stated as belief.

title: Azure Cosmos DB - North Europe
root_cause_quote: Our frontend load balancing procedure had a regression that did not factor in the effect of a reduction in available cluster capacity, due to ongoing maintenance. This surfaced during an ongoing platform maintenance event in one of the frontend clusters in the North Europe region, causing the availability issues described above.
detection_note: Our monitors alerted us of the impact on this cluster.
notes: Regression (deploy date not given) surfaced by routine maintenance; change_triggered=true for the maintenance.

title: Canonical Ubuntu issue impacted VMs and AKS
root_cause_quote: At 06:00 UTC on 30 August 2022, a Canonical Ubuntu security update was published – so Azure VMs running Ubuntu 18.04 (bionic) with unattended-upgrade enabled started to download and install the new packages, including systemd version 237-3ubuntu10.54.
detection_note: Multiple Azure teams detected the issue shortly after the packages were published via production alerts, including our AKS and Azure Container Apps service teams.
notes: Third-party systemd race bug wiped DNS config on Ubuntu 18.04 VMs via unattended upgrades; hit AKS and Azure Monitor.

title: Datacenter power event - West US 2
root_cause_quote: The initial trigger to this event was when a high voltage static wire (used to help protect transmission lines against lightning strikes) failed. When the static wire failed, it created a voltage surge on the 230kV lines, causing breakers at two substations (approximately 30 miles apart) within the utility power grid to open.
detection_note: This event was first detected by our EPMS (Electrical Power Monitoring System) in West US 2, which in turn notified our datacenter team of the utility loss issue, and then of equipment failure issues.
notes: Region-wide utility loss; rack UPS and UPS battery failures in two datacenters.

title: Azure Key Vault - Provisioning Failures
root_cause_quote: During the incident, a backend service that Azure Key Vault relies on, became unhealthy due to an unexpected spike in traffic during scheduled hardware maintenance, which caused a build-up of requests in the queue, resulting in high latencies to fulfil new certificate creation requests.
notes: Certificate provisioning backlog blocked provisioning of many services; maintenance role in the capacity loss not detailed.

title: Azure Communication Services - Multiple Regions
root_cause_quote: At 18:00 UTC on 12 Aug 2022, to meet the increased demand of requests, the database processing capacity was increased. This change in database capacity inadvertently exposed a latent code bug for the resource provider, which resulted in a functional difference in the number of database results being returned against what could be processed by the resource provider.
detection_note: Automated alerting indicated several failures for different ACS API requests made by customers.
notes: Cosmos DB capacity increase exposed RP paging bug; ACS authentication failed globally; rollback not supported.

title: Network Connectivity Issues
root_cause_quote: Starting at 08:00 UTC on 29 July, the Azure WAN began to experience a sudden and significant increase of traffic, upwards of 60 Tbps in additional traffic compared to the normal levels of traffic carried on the network.
detection_note: Detected immediately; automated remediation triggered but could not keep up.
notes: Traffic reached 10-15x prior peaks; WAN routers overloaded. Source of the surge not stated.

title: SQL Database - West Europe
root_cause_quote: An operator error led to an incorrect action being performed in close sequence on all four persisted metadata caches. The action resulted in a configuration change that made the caches unavailable to the regional gateway processes.
detection_note: This regional incident was detected by our availability monitors, and we were on the investigation bridge within 13 minutes of customer impact.
notes: SQL gateways lost routing metadata; telemetry overload delayed customer notifications and auto-failover.

title: Wide Area Network - Multiple Regions
root_cause_quote: We have determined that one of several WAN routers handling traffic transiting this area experienced a partial hardware failure, which caused it to route improperly 0.4% of the packets it normally handles.
detection_note: Since end users experienced this issue intermittently, this was characterized as a ‘gray’ failure so alerting was not immediately able to identify that there was an issue.
notes: London WAN router line card gray failure.

title: Azure Software Load Balancer - Multiple Regions
root_cause_quote: Upon investigating this issue, we identified a change in our latest code deployment which caused some MUX instances to store the backend DIPs in a different order.
notes: Only LBs with >15 DIPs; broke flow affinity for Azure Firewall and private/service endpoints.

title: Datacenter cooling event - East US 2
root_cause_quote: Microsoft experienced an unplanned power oscillation in one of our datacenters within one of our Availability Zones in the East US 2 region. Components of our redundant power system created unexpected electrical transients, which resulted in the Air Handling Units (AHUs) detecting a potential fault, and therefore shutting themselves down pending a manual reset.
detection_note: As soon as the AHUs shut themselves down as a result of the power disturbance, alerts notified our onsite datacenter operators.
notes: UPS transients shut down cooling; thermal shutdown of storage/compute in one AZ.

title: Azure Active Directory Sign In logs
root_cause_quote: As part of continuous service improvements, a recent change to the underlying infrastructure that was intended to optimize performance, inadvertently caused the observed impact.
detection_note: While this issue was detected by our telemetry, service health degradation was only detected in the final phase of the rollout.
notes: Change type not specified (classed as deploy); rollback failed, hotfix mitigated.

title: Service Management Operation Errors Across Azure Services in East US 2
root_cause_quote: The underlying issue was a retry storm triggered by the zonal failure of a related Allocator service.
notes: Backlog exposed .NET GC/process-wide lock interaction; Allocator failure cause not stated.

title: Azure AD B2C – Authentication Failures and Error Notifications
root_cause_quote: The service experienced a significant increase in workload in the affected region during a planned maintenance operation.
notes: Short RCA; link between maintenance and workload not explained.

title: Azure Resource Manager - Service Management Operation Failures
root_cause_quote: A synchronization issue occurred between backend components used to permit certain ARM requests. A configuration change was applied to these backend components, which resulted in some instances of the ARM service becoming unreachable, causing errors for a subset of operation requests.
notes: Azure Government ARM; fixed by hotfix.

title: SQL Database and App Service - West Europe
root_cause_quote: Due to a memory hardware failure in a network router, a control plane/data plane synchronization process in that router failed during a regular automated maintenance operation.
detection_note: The mitigation took longer than expected as the impacted device was going through automated maintenance, during which alerts were suppressed.
notes: Router dropped packets for up to 12% of flows during firmware upgrade; alerts suppressed during maintenance.

title: Azure SQL DB and Cosmos DB Unavailable
root_cause_quote: A race condition in the underlying Remote Procedure Call (RPC) mechanism caused the network control plane channel in some cases to not pick up the rotated certificate, leading to connectivity failures once the certificate expired.
notes: Fix already shipped to general fleet in January but deferred for SQL/Cosmos DB hardware generation.

title: Azure AD - Service Management Failures
root_cause_quote: As part of planned maintenance, a change to a dependency was rolled out which affected the availability of the Azure AD REST API service.
notes: Caches delayed impact; overall availability stayed at 99.996%.

title: Azure Resource Manager - Issues with management and resource operations
root_cause_quote: A code modification which started rolling out on 6 Jan 2022 exposed a latent defect in the infrastructure used to process long running operations (informally, "jobs").
notes: Job execution shifted to paired regions, then spread as they got the code; broad ARM delays.

title: Azure Cosmos DB - East US
root_cause_quote: During this incident, the timer callback on one of the nodes was fired multiple times at a frequency higher than intended. This resulted in the node's neighbors getting incorrectly reported as unavailable.
notes: Service Fabric arbitrators trusted false reports until cluster quorum was lost; fixed by rebooting culprit node.

title: Azure Active Directory - Experiencing sign in issues when attempting to access Azure, Dynamics 365, and/or Microsoft 365 Services
root_cause_quote: A regular operating system (OS) update was deployed to endpoints of a backend service in the Azure AD authentication stack, which interacted with the service in an unexpected way, making the service on the updated endpoints unresponsive.
notes: Health-monitoring gap let rollout reach all redundant endpoints; latent circuit-breaker issue widened impact. MSA impact from 00:11.

title: Azure Data Factory V2 - West Europe
root_cause_quote: We determined a backend service, responsible for processing API requests became unhealthy. Retry logic from ADF, coupled with this unhealthy service, resulted in a rare combination of transient conditions and lead to additional errors.
notes: Reason the backend service became unhealthy is not stated.

title: Errors connecting to SCM App Service and/or Azure Functions deployments
root_cause_quote: As part of introducing certain resiliency measures, a configuration change was implemented to create a redundant Domain Name Resolution zone for App Service SCM endpoints. However, due to a misconfiguration, this change incorrectly affected the name resolution for App Service SCM endpoint, which resulted in a subset of our customers not being able to connect to the SCM endpoints of the service.
detection_note: Engineering was engaged upon receiving reports of failure.
notes: DNS zone change; recovery depended on client TTLs.

title: Azure Active Directory - Issues when attempting to authenticate
root_cause_quote: The engineering team has determined that an underlying code defect triggered some service nodes to experience a shortage of outbound ports to complete network tasks.
notes: Azure AD B2C Australia; two impact windows.

title: Intermittent Failures When Accessing or Using Access Panel
root_cause_quote: On 09 Nov 2021 between 03:00 and 05:30 UTC, a code change to Access Panel was deployed and introduced an unrelated bug impacting a small subset of customers.
detection_note: The issue was detected by automation at 14:09 UTC on 09 Nov 2021 and engineers were engaged at 14:14 UTC.
notes: Bug led to failover to Central US scaled for off-hours; business-hours ramp outpaced autoscaling.

title: Virtual Machines
root_cause_quote: At approximately 06:27 UTC, tooling provided an ARM template for use in performing these migrations. This tooling did not consider an edge case and as an unintended consequence marked the Windows VM Agent extension as visible to the publishing subscription only in the ARM regional service after migration.
notes: Classic-to-ARM publisher migration hid the VM Agent extension; Windows VM operations failed.

title: Service availability issue - Brazil South
root_cause_quote: During this maintenance activity, a technician was executing a change that impacted the incorrect set of cables.
detection_note: On 23 Jul 2021, at 19:00 UTC, we received an alert from our health monitoring that there were network connectivity issues in the Brazil South region.
notes: Wrong cables disturbed during planned maintenance in Brazil South.

title: Google Cloud Storage customers are experiencing elevated latencies and error rates when performing upload or write operations.
root_cause_quote: A traffic sorting optimization intended to address localized capacity constraints caused severe resource exhaustion on specific backend storage nodes in the affected region.
detection_note: The issue was initially detected by Google engineering teams actively monitoring system telemetry early in the incident window.
notes: Preliminary report; GCS us-central1 write errors; change type of the optimization not specified; concurrent metadata DB update also rolled back

title: Multiple products in us-central1-b are experiencing network service degradation.
root_cause_quote: The event was triggered by the inadvertent physical disconnection of network fiber-optic cables during routine hardware maintenance.
detection_note: The issue was detected immediately by automated network loss monitoring systems as well as proactive probes, which rapidly engaged the network engineering and incident response teams.
notes: Router transceiver upgrade issued without one-router-at-a-time sequencing; us-central1-b isolated

title: We are investigating an issue where customers may experience timeouts, service degradations, errors, and elevated latencies across multiple products in the us-west1 region.
root_cause_quote: The disruption originated during scheduled fiber optic maintenance, which unexpectedly compromised network capacity between data centers within the us-west1 region. Automated rerouting mechanisms failed to properly redistribute traffic to alternate capacity, resulting in network congestion as volumes exceeded available bandwidth in the affected area.
detection_note: Internal monitoring systems initially detected widespread service anomalies and alerted Google engineers
notes: us-west1 congestion cascaded to Spanner, UMS, GCS, IAM, PD, GKE

title: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE), Google Cloud NetApp Volumes, and Bare Metal Solutions (BMS) services are experiencing a service outage in europe-west4-a due to a cooling failure.
root_cause_quote: A regional data center hosting services in europe-west4-a experienced an upstream voltage transient affecting both utility power feeds A and B. During this event, the utility breakers on both A and B feeds tripped and initiated the transfer to the back-up power source DRUPS (Diesel Rotary Uninterruptible Power Supply).
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the infrastructure power loss on Wednesday, 15 July 2026 at 16:30 US/Pacific and subsequent increase in data hall temperatures at 17:44 US/Pacific via our automated monitoring and telemetry
notes: DRUPS side A failed, one row lost both feeds, chiller pumps failed to restart; GCVE/NetApp/BMS

title: Google Cloud VMware Engine (GCVE) Stretched Cluster customers are experiencing zonal outages impacting network connectivity across multiple regions.
root_cause_quote: A network configuration update intended to prepare the cloud network infrastructure for new capabilities was deployed to the foundational network control plane. While the configuration payload itself was structurally valid, it exposed an implementation gap within the control plane's routing logic.
detection_note: Because the control plane remained healthy, standard failover mechanisms failed to detect that the selective private IP range used for inter-zonal data tunneling was being dropped.
notes: GCVE Stretched Cluster private IP range dropped; passed payload validation

title: Vertex AI Gemini API customers experienced increased error rates when accessing the global endpoint.
root_cause_quote: This incident was caused by a configuration change to a safety filtering service that supports all Gemini models.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the issue via our automated monitoring system on Friday, 27 February 2026 04:54 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation.
notes: Vertex Gemini API 429/503s; rolled back config

title: We are investigating elevated error rates with multiple products in us-east1
root_cause_quote: The service interruption was triggered by a procedural error during a planned hardware replacement in our datacenter. An incorrect physical disconnection was made to the active network switch serving our control plane, rather than the redundant unit scheduled for removal.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage by our monitoring system on 18 July 2025 07:06 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation.
notes: us-east1 control plane partition; fail-open then topology change caused stale topology

title: Multiple GCP products are experiencing Service issues.
root_cause_quote: On June 12, 2025 at ~10:45am PDT, a policy change was inserted into the regional Spanner tables that Service Control uses for policies. Given the global nature of quota management, this metadata was replicated globally within seconds. This policy data contained unintended blank fields.
detection_note: Within 2 minutes, our Site Reliability Engineering team was triaging the incident.
notes: Blank fields hit a null-pointer path in a May 29 Service Control release that lacked feature-flag protection; global 503s

title: Google Compute Engine (GCE) issue impacting multiple dependent GCP services across zones
root_cause_quote: A recently deployed configuration change to a Google Compute Engine (GCE) component mistakenly disabled a feature flag that controlled how VM instance states are reported to other components. Safety checks intended to ensure gradual rollout of this type of change failed to be triggered, resulting in an unplanned rapid rollout of the change.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage via internal monitoring on 19 May 2025, at 21:08 US/Pacific, and immediately started an investigation.
notes: Spot VM termination backlog degraded all VM types

title: Customers are experiencing connectivity issues with multiple Google Cloud services in zone us-east5-c
root_cause_quote: The root cause of the service disruption was a loss of utility power in the affected zone. This power outage triggered a cascading failure within the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) system responsible for maintaining power to the zone during such events.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the incident from our internal monitoring alerts at 12:54 US/Pacific on Saturday, 29 March and immediately started an investigation.
notes: us-east5-c; UPS critical battery failure

title: Apigee customers may experience unable to login to Admin UI portal.
root_cause_quote: From preliminary analysis root cause appears to be due certificate expiration.
notes: Apigee Admin UI login; one-line preliminary cause only

title: SIEM Dashboards and SOAR Advanced Dashboards for Google Security Operations (SecOps) were unavailable.
root_cause_quote: From preliminary analysis, the root cause of the issue is related to a revocation of associated internal looker licenses - all revoked licenses were restored to mitigate an issue.
notes: SecOps SIEM/SOAR dashboards; preliminary; who/why of revocation not stated

title: Chronicle Security - WORKSPACE_ACTIVITY data ingestion observed delays in asia-southeast1 & asia-south1 regions
root_cause_quote: Chronicle Security WORKSPACE_ACTIVITY data ingestion observed delays in asia-southeast1 and asia-south1 regions for 13 hours, 20 minutes due to network connectivity issues between the trans-Pacific regions.
notes: Mini report; underlying network cause not given

title: Appsheet is unavailable in us-east4 and europe-west4
root_cause_quote: A database schema migration in production triggered a cascading incident. The migration caused failures and timeouts on the primary database, disrupting most AppSheet operations and preventing apps loading for users in us-east4 and europe-west4.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage via an automated alert on 24 January 2025 09:42 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation.
notes: Retry surge then overloaded auth database

title: We are experiencing an issue with Chronicle Security
root_cause_quote: From preliminary analysis, the issue was due to a software defect introduced by a recent service update that had been rolled out to non-US regions.
notes: SecOps SOAR 403s for non-admin users; rolled back

title: Multiple regions completely blocked for subscribe for Pubsub
root_cause_quote: From 8 January 2025 06:54 to 07:30 US/Pacific, a bad service configuration change, which unintentionally over-restricted the permission to access this database, was rolled out to multiple regions. The issue did not surface in our pre-production environment due to a mismatch in the configuration between the two environments.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage via internal telemetry on 8 January 2025 07:03 US/Pacific, 9 minutes after impact started.
notes: Pub/Sub regional metadata DB permissions; multi-region

title: We are experiencing an issue with Vertex Gemini API in Asia
root_cause_quote: root cause of the incident is stemmed from a Vertex service dependency ending up in a bad state due to a configuration process.
notes: Vertex Gemini API asia; vague mini report

title: Vertex Gemini API serving the gemini-1.5-flash model may experience elevated latency or errors in multiregions/us
root_cause_quote: root cause of the issue was a significant increase in decode processing load stemming from a large spike in response content heavy traffic.
notes: gemini-1.5-flash-002 multiregion-us

title: We are investigating elevated error rates and latency for streaming ingestion into BigQuery
root_cause_quote: This backend service enforces a limit on the number of such concurrent connections for flow control and a bug in its mechanism prevented backends from accepting new requests once this limit was reached.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage by our internal monitoring system on Monday, 9 December 2024 at 09:33 US/Pacific and immediately started an investigation.
notes: BigQuery streaming backend; triggered by slightly higher than usual customer traffic

title: We experienced elevated errors with BigQuery accessing Google Drive.
root_cause_quote: This disruption of data export functionality was triggered by the deletion of an internal project containing essential API keys.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the service degrading via a support case on 4 December 2024, at approximately 14:21 US/Pacific when users began experiencing failures in data export operations.
notes: BigQuery-Drive; project wrongly classified abandoned; API key = credential

title: Multiple GCP Products including Google Cloud Networking, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Cloud Load Balancing are experiencing issues in the asia-southeast2 region
root_cause_quote: On 16 November 2024 at 00:47 US/Pacific, a combination of fiber failures and a network equipment fault led to reduced network capacity between the asia-southeast2 region and other GCP regions.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted of these failures as soon as they occurred and were working with urgency on remediating these fiber failures but had not yet completed full recovery.
notes: Two fiber cuts plus a latent router software defect exhausted capacity buffers

title: Issues opening cases
root_cause_quote: The outage was triggered by a vendor-initiated change that impacted the performance of our support ticket persistence layer.
detection_note: Our monitoring systems detected elevated error rates and, at 22:09 US/Pacific, alerted our engineering team, who immediately started an investigation with the vendor.
notes: Support case tool; change made by vendor, not Google

title: All the impacted GCP products in australia-southeast2 have recovered.
root_cause_quote: On Tuesday, 29 October 2024 at 16:21 US/Pacific, a power voltage swell event impacted the Network Point of Presence (POP) infrastructure in one of the campuses supporting the australia-southeast2 region, causing networking devices to unexpectedly reboot.
detection_note: Google engineers were already working on remediating the two fiber failures when they were alerted to the network disruption caused by the voltage swell via an internal monitoring alert on Tuesday, 29 October 2024 16:29 US/Pacific
notes: Voltage tolerance mismatch rack vs UPS; plus two fiber failures

title: [Mandiant.com](http://Mandiant.com) was inaccessible globally.
root_cause_quote: root cause of the issues is an inappropriate redirect rule, which was implemented as part of an ongoing procedure to assess the effectiveness of an upcoming transition.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the incident from our internal monitoring alerts at 14:29 US/Pacific on Monday, 28 October 2024 and immediately started an investigation.
notes: mandiant.com redirected to another site

title: Cloud Build - builds execution is degraded in us-central1
root_cause_quote: The root cause of the issue is Cloud Build's failure to degrade gracefully upon being throttled by its GCE API quota in the us-central1 region. As a result of being throttled, the Cloud Build component responsible for managing worker pools initiated multiple retries due to an incorrect configuration, further exacerbating the quota exhaustion and completely preventing the creation of new worker instances in the region.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to the outage from an internal monitoring alert at 02:31 US/Pacific on Friday 25 October, 2024 and immediately started an investigation.
notes: Quota exhaustion amplified by retry misconfig

title: Multiple GCP services impacted in the europe-west3-c zone
root_cause_quote: On 23 October 2024, at 18:22 US/Pacific time, an electrical arc flash occurred in one of the europe-west3-c zone's power distribution units, resulting in a partial power outage.
detection_note: Google engineers were alerted to VM failures in europe-west3-c zone at 18:39 US/Pacific on 23 October 2024, and immediately launched an investigation.
notes: Cooling also affected; equipment shut down

title: Large Vertex Model Garden Deployment may experience failures.
root_cause_quote: root cause of the issue is an internal storage provisioning configuration error that was implemented as part of a recent change.
notes: Vertex Model Garden large deployments; config rolled back

title: Case creation may fail intermittently with an error
root_cause_quote: From preliminary analysis, we believe the cause of the issue was a recent change to Google Support’s ticket persistence layer. The change granted a subsystem unbounded resource consumption, impacting user requests.
notes: Support case creation; preliminary; change type (config vs code) not specified

title: Multiple GCP products impacted in us-west2 region / us-west2-a zone
root_cause_quote: A mismatch in configuration between two components of Google’s internal cluster management system resulted in a failure of the cluster service discovery component. This failure was triggered by a software rollout within the cluster management system that was believed to be non-impactful to operating jobs.
notes: us-west2-a; fixed by correcting a file path

title: Customers may experience intermittent issues with support case creation
root_cause_quote: Beginning at 14:18 on Wednesday, 02 October 2024, an existing internal Google reporting service that integrates with the ticket persistence layer responded to an increase in data volume by rapidly ramping traffic. Due to a latent issue in the reporting service, it sent traffic in a way that bypassed normal backpressure signals.
detection_note: As each impact period was short, internal monitoring metrics for the support UI did not reach alarm thresholds until 15:01.
notes: Support case creation; internal client bypassed backpressure

title: Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019
root_cause_quote: On July 2, we deployed a new rule in our WAF Managed Rules that caused CPUs to become exhausted on every CPU core that handles HTTP/HTTPS traffic on the Cloudflare network worldwide.
detection_note: Three minutes later the first PagerDuty page went out indicating a fault with the WAF.
notes: Backtracking regex in a WAF rule pushed globally (rules bypassed staged rollout); 27 min global 502s.

title: Cloudflare outage on July 17, 2020
root_cause_quote: This configuration contained an error that caused all traffic across our backbone to be sent to Atlanta. This quickly overwhelmed the Atlanta router and caused Cloudflare network locations connected to the backbone to fail.
notes: Manual router config change in Atlanta during backbone congestion response; ~50% traffic drop for 27 min.

title: PIPEFAIL: How a missing shell option slowed Cloudflare down
root_cause_quote: A manual rollback inadvertently triggered the thundering herd problem, which overwhelmed the Addressing API. We have since significantly scaled out the Addressing API, so that it can handle high request rates if it ever again has to. An error in a Kubernetes cron job caused invalid data to be written to Quicksilver.
detection_note: Within minutes of starting the second batch of rollbacks, alerts started firing.
notes: Manual rollback + cron job lacking pipefail wrote empty config; dosd failed, requests delayed up to 5s.

title: Cloudflare outage on June 21, 2022
root_cause_quote: While deploying a change to our prefix advertisement policies, a re-ordering of terms caused us to withdraw a critical subset of prefixes.
detection_note: 06:32: Internal Cloudflare incident declared (5 min after impact began at 06:27).
notes: BGP policy change on MCP spines took 19 busiest data centers offline; 06:27-07:42 UTC.

title: Partial Cloudflare outage on October 25, 2022
root_cause_quote: At 08:40 UTC, a software release of a CDN component containing a bug began slowly rolling out.
detection_note: We started an investigation after receiving customer reports of an intermittent increase in 530s after the faulty component was released to a subset of data centers.
notes: Tiered Cache release bug caused 530s (~5% peak); report says impact almost six hours total; 08:40-18:04 window.

title: Cloudflare incident on January 24, 2023
root_cause_quote: The change inadvertently overwrote other metadata about the service tokens and rendered the tokens of impacted accounts invalid for the duration of the incident.
notes: Access release overwrote service token metadata; invalid credentials broke internal accounts powering Workers/Zero Trust; 121 min.

title: 1.1.1.1 lookup failures on October 4, 2023
root_cause_quote: However, the 1.1.1.1 resolver systems that make use of that data had problems parsing the ZONEMD record. Because zones must be loaded and served in their entirety, the system’s failure to parse ZONEMD meant the new versions of the root zone were not used in Cloudflare’s resolver systems.
detection_note: 7:57: First external reports of unexpected SERVFAILs started coming in. 8:03: Internal Cloudflare incident declared.
notes: Parser couldn't handle new ZONEMD record added to root zone by third party; stale zone's DNSSEC signatures expired -> SERVFAILs.

title: Cloudflare incident on October 30, 2023
root_cause_quote: In this incident, the service was deployed and tested in staging. But because of the deployment automation bug, when promoting to production, a script that had been deployed to the staging account was incorrectly referenced instead of the pre-production version on the production account.
detection_note: Wrong-destination routing during progressive rollout triggered alerting and the decision to roll back.
notes: Workers KV deployment tool bug pointed production at staging build; KV returned 401s, breaking Pages, Access, Turnstile etc. for 37 min.

title: Post mortem on the Cloudflare Control Plane and Analytics Outage
root_cause_quote: On November 2 at 08:50 UTC Portland General Electric (PGE), the utility company that services PDX-04, had an unplanned maintenance event affecting one of their independent power feeds into the building. That event shut down one feed into PDX-04.
notes: Flexential PDX data center power loss; control plane/analytics down, non-HA dependencies exposed; mostly restored via DR by 17:57 UTC.

title: Major data center power failure (again): Cloudflare Code Orange tested
root_cause_quote: On March 26, 2024, at 14:58 UTC, PDX01 experienced a total loss of power to Cloudflare’s physical infrastructure following a reportedly simultaneous failure of four Flexential-owned and operated switchboards serving all of Cloudflare’s cages.
detection_note: Just like in November 2023, we were alerted immediately that we had lost connectivity to our PDX01 data center.
notes: Same facility lost power again; automatic failover restored API/dashboard by 15:05 UTC, some services needed manual recovery.

title: Cloudflare incident on June 20, 2024
root_cause_quote: A new Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) mitigation mechanism deployed between 14:14 and 17:06 UTC triggered a latent bug in our rate limiting system that allowed a specific form of HTTP request to cause a process handling it to enter an infinite loop between 17:47 and 19:27 UTC
detection_note: 18:04 Incident declared automatically based on detected high CPU load
notes: New DDoS rule exposed latent rate-limiter infinite loop; plus separate automated reroute causing backbone congestion; 114 min.

title: Cloudflare incident on September 17, 2024
root_cause_quote: At 2024-09-17 17:51 UTC, fifteen IPv4 prefixes corresponding to the addresses that were thought to be safely unused were withdrawn using BGP.
detection_note: At 18:36, Cloudflare received escalations from two customers, and an incident was declared.
notes: Routine IPv4 renumbering/prefix withdrawal; earlier code change had left 1,661 sites on old addresses; earlier alerts at 17:57 dismissed as expected.

title: Cloudflare incident on November 14, 2024, resulting in lost logs
root_cause_quote: Every few minutes, a separate system re-generates the configuration used by Logfwdr to decide which logs need to be forwarded. A bug in this system resulted in a blank configuration being provided to Logfwdr.
detection_note: Team noticed the mistake and reverted the change in under five minutes, but fail-open behaviour had already overloaded Buftee.
notes: Change for new Logpush dataset produced blank config; fail-open sent all logs, overloaded misconfigured Buftee; ~55% of logs lost.

title: Cloudflare incident on February 6, 2025
root_cause_quote: The incident occurred due to human error and insufficient validation safeguards during a routine abuse remediation for a report about a phishing site hosted on R2. The action taken on the complaint resulted in an advanced product disablement action on the site that led to disabling the production R2 Gateway service responsible for the R2 API.
detection_note: Critical R2 alerts begin to fire due to our service no longer responding to our health checks.
notes: Abuse-remediation action disabled the production R2 Gateway; R2 and dependents (Stream, Images, Cache Reserve) down 59 min.

title: Cloudflare incident on March 21, 2025
root_cause_quote: While rotating credentials used by the R2 Gateway service (R2's API frontend) to authenticate with our storage infrastructure, the R2 engineering team inadvertently deployed the new credentials (ID and key pair) to a development instance of the service instead of production.
detection_note: R2 global availability alerts are triggered (indicating 2% of error budget burn rate).
notes: Credential rotation pushed new keys to dev; old keys deleted; 100% R2 writes failed for 67 min.

title: Cloudflare service outage June 12, 2025
root_cause_quote: The cause of this outage was due to a failure in the underlying storage infrastructure used by our Workers KV service, which is a critical dependency for many Cloudflare products and relied upon for configuration, authentication and asset delivery across the affected services. Part of this infrastructure is backed by a third-party cloud provider, which experienced an outage today and directly impacted availability of our KV service.
detection_note: Cloudflare Access team received an alert due to a rapid increase in error rates.
notes: Third-party cloud storage backing Workers KV failed; Access, WARP, Gateway, Turnstile etc. impacted for 2h28m.

title: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 Incident on July 14, 2025
root_cause_quote: On June 6, during a release to prepare a service topology for a future DLS service, a configuration error was introduced: the prefixes associated with the 1.1.1.1 Resolver service were inadvertently included alongside the prefixes that were intended for the new DLS service.
detection_note: Internal service health alerts begin to fire for the 1.1.1.1 Resolver
notes: Dormant topology misconfig; July 14 config change triggered global refresh that withdrew 1.1.1.1 prefixes; 62 min global resolver outage.

title: Cloudflare incident on August 21, 2025
root_cause_quote: The incident was a result of a surge of traffic from a single customer that overloaded Cloudflare's links with AWS us-east-1. It was a network congestion event, not an attack or a BGP hijack.
detection_note: Network team is alerted to internal congestion in Ashburn (IAD)
notes: Regional congestion on Cloudflare-AWS us-east-1 links; 16:27-20:18 UTC.

title: A deep dive into Cloudflare’s September 12, 2025 dashboard and API outage
root_cause_quote: The incident’s impact stemmed from several issues, but the immediate trigger was a bug in the dashboard. This bug caused repeated, unnecessary calls to the Tenant Service API.
notes: Dashboard release with React useEffect loop plus Tenant Service deploy overloaded API authorization; 17:57-19:12 UTC.

title: Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025
root_cause_quote: Instead, it was triggered by a change to one of our database systems' permissions which caused the database to output multiple entries into a “feature file” used by our Bot Management system. That feature file, in turn, doubled in size.
detection_note: The first automated test detected the issue at 11:31 and manual investigation started at 11:32.
notes: ClickHouse permissions change doubled Bot Management feature file past proxy limit; core traffic restored 14:30, all by 17:06; initially suspected DDoS.

title: Cloudflare outage on December 5, 2025
root_cause_quote: This second change of turning off our WAF testing tool was implemented using our global configuration system. This system does not perform gradual rollouts, but rather propagates changes within seconds to the entire fleet of servers in our network
detection_note: 08:50 INCIDENT declared via automated alerts (impact began 08:47).
notes: Global config change disabling WAF test tool hit a years-old FL1 proxy bug; ~28% of HTTP traffic got 500s for ~25 min.

title: What came first: the CNAME or the A record?
root_cause_quote: While making some improvements to lower the memory usage of our cache implementation, we introduced a subtle change to CNAME record ordering. The change was introduced on December 2, 2025, released to our testing environment on December 10, and began deployment on January 7, 2026.
